title: Solara Elysian Production EV Sedan Release
short_summary: Mock public-source record for a production EV sedan using a low nose, full-width lighting, and restrained surfacing to signal efficient premium mobility.
design_observations: The sedan shifts identity away from grille mass and toward a continuous lamp graphic.
The greenhouse reads elongated because the DLO stretches cleanly into a dark rear-quarter insert.
Flush handles and reduced cutlines support the aerodynamic story without making the body anonymous.
proportion_observation: Long wheelbase, short overhangs, and a low cowl create an EV-native premium sedan stance.
volume_observation: The main body volume is calm and almost monolithic, with the cabin treated as a light glass canopy.
surface_observation: Soft crown sections replace hard shoulder lines, relying on reflections to define the body side.
graphic_observation: The front and rear full-width light bars are the strongest recognisable brand graphics.
brand_language_observation: Solara's mock language emphasizes quiet technology rather than aggressive performance decoration.
designer_note: Human review should verify whether the lighting signature is described by the source as brand identity or only shown visually.

title: Kanso Serein Luxury Sedan Interior Direction
short_summary: Mock production sedan note focused on warm minimalism, layered textiles, indirect lighting, and selective physical controls.
design_observations: The IP uses horizontal layers to make the cabin feel wider and calmer.
Low-gloss materials reduce glare and support a restful premium impression.
Frequently used functions remain tactile, preventing the interface from feeling screen-only.
proportion_observation: A long cabin and low beltline make the sedan read as chauffeur-friendly rather than driver-only.
volume_observation: Interior volumes are organized as stacked planes rather than a single sculptural dashboard mass.
surface_observation: Soft-touch panels use low-contrast transitions to avoid visual clutter.
graphic_observation: Ambient light bands act as the primary cabin graphic and help define zones.
brand_language_observation: Kanso's mock language frames luxury as calm usability and tactile restraint.
designer_note: Check that any future material claims are sourced from official CMF notes or verified interviews.

title: Rangewell Trailmark Adventure Pickup Release
short_summary: Mock pickup release using modular graphics, squared wheel arches, and visible recovery elements to express utility without excessive decoration.
design_observations: Squared wheel openings frame the tire as a functional object.
Graphic modules align with repairable or replaceable body zones.
The upper body remains clean so functional details carry the rugged message.
proportion_observation: An upright cab, short front overhang, and visually heavy rear bed create a work-first stance.
volume_observation: The body is divided into robust modules that suggest durability and serviceability.
surface_observation: Flat upper surfaces and chamfered lower sections keep the vehicle tool-like rather than decorative.
graphic_observation: Contrast corner blocks and tow-point accents provide the most immediate rugged cues.
brand_language_observation: Rangewell's mock language prioritizes functional honesty and visible protection.
designer_note: Do not imply off-road capability beyond what the source explicitly states.

title: Aurora A9 E-SUV Concept Surface Study
short_summary: Mock concept SUV highlighting calm surfacing, a floating roof, and a reduced front mask for quiet electric confidence.
design_observations: The body side avoids heavy character lines and uses light catchers above the rocker.
A dark floating roof graphic visually lowers the greenhouse.
The front mask shifts recognition toward lighting and badge placement.
proportion_observation: A long wheelbase and low visual beltline help a large SUV read lighter than its segment suggests.
volume_observation: The upper cabin appears detached from a stable lower body volume through the floating roof treatment.
surface_observation: Broad, unbroken door surfaces communicate premium calm and reduce visual noise.
graphic_observation: Thin lamps and a horizontal lower intake create width without grille dominance.
brand_language_observation: Aurora's mock direction moves from chrome-heavy premium cues to light-led EV identity.
designer_note: Useful candidate for a social draft about how EV SUVs reduce visual mass.

title: Nomi Loop Urban EV Concept
short_summary: Mock city EV concept focused on friendly proportions, protective corner graphics, and cabin-forward packaging for dense urban mobility.
design_observations: Short overhangs and a tall cabin maximize perceived interior room.
Rounded lamp modules reduce aggression and make the car approachable.
Contrast-color corner blocks communicate durability and repair-zone logic.
proportion_observation: The mono-volume silhouette puts cabin space ahead of traditional hood prestige.
volume_observation: A simple one-box volume makes the small footprint feel intentional rather than compromised.
surface_observation: Large-radius surfaces avoid tension and support the approachable character.
graphic_observation: Friendly round-corner lighting and bumper patches are the main emotional graphics.
brand_language_observation: Nomi's mock language uses softness and replaceable-looking details to make urban mobility feel low-stress.
designer_note: Good candidate for a Xiaohongshu explainer about why small EVs often look friendly.

title: Vitesse R12 Heritage Performance Coupe Concept
short_summary: Mock coupe language study balancing heritage proportions with modern aero details, including a pronounced dash-to-axle ratio and precision-cut vents.
design_observations: The long hood and rear-set cabin create a classic performance proportion.
Technical vent inserts modernize the silhouette without overpowering it.
Rear haunch emphasis gives the car a planted powertrain narrative.
proportion_observation: The dash-to-axle distance and rearward cabin are the primary heritage signals.
volume_observation: A slim cabin sits above a muscular rear body, emphasizing stored energy over cabin volume.
surface_observation: Taut fender surfaces and controlled highlights communicate performance precision.
graphic_observation: Small aero blades and vent openings provide modern detail against a classic silhouette.
brand_language_observation: Vitesse's mock language preserves recognisable sports-car cues while adding aero-functional graphics.
designer_note: Avoid framing the concept as production-confirmed unless a future source verifies that status.

title: Interview: Lumen Design Lead on Light-Led EV Identity
short_summary: Mock interview summary about using lighting architecture as a primary brand signature as EV front ends become more closed and simplified.
design_observations: The interview frames lighting as a substitute for grille recognition.
Night-time recognisability becomes part of brand strategy, not only safety compliance.
The design team discusses balancing digital expression with long-term brand consistency.
proportion_observation: The interview suggests that reduced front openings make the vehicle's width and stance more dependent on lamp placement.
volume_observation: Closed front volumes require subtle shaping so the fascia does not become blank or appliance-like.
surface_observation: Smooth front surfaces need controlled highlight breaks to support perceived precision.
graphic_observation: Lighting graphics carry both functional and emotional identity roles.
brand_language_observation: Lumen's mock language treats illumination as the core recognisable asset for EVs.
designer_note: Future real interviews require quote verification and clear separation between paraphrase and direct quotation.

title: Interview: Oriq CMF Team on Sustainable Touchpoints
short_summary: Mock interview summary covering recycled textiles, lower-gloss surfaces, and how sustainable materials should still feel durable and premium.
design_observations: The CMF team emphasizes that sustainability cues must be tangible rather than purely claimed.
Lower-gloss finishes can communicate refinement and reduce screen glare.
Material transitions are used to explain where occupants touch the vehicle most.
proportion_observation: Interior proportion is discussed through occupant reach zones rather than exterior stance.
volume_observation: Door and dashboard volumes are broken into touch, storage, and display layers.
surface_observation: Textile grain and matte coatings are used to make surfaces feel less synthetic.
graphic_observation: Material boundary lines become subtle graphics that guide interaction.
brand_language_observation: Oriq's mock language connects sustainability with durability and everyday tactility.
designer_note: Any sustainability claim must be checked against the original source and not amplified beyond evidence.

title: Atlas Updates Adventure EV Design Language
short_summary: Mock brand-language update describing a shift from combustion-era toughness cues to cleaner EV adventure graphics and modular protection zones.
design_observations: The brand keeps upright stance cues while reducing faux vents and unnecessary texture.
Protection zones are expressed as replaceable modules rather than decorative cladding.
Lighting becomes a technical signature across different body styles.
proportion_observation: Atlas retains vertical stance and wheel emphasis to preserve adventure credibility.
volume_observation: Body volumes become cleaner and more slab-sided as EV packaging reduces front mechanical drama.
surface_observation: Broad surfaces are interrupted only where protection or access is visually useful.
graphic_observation: Modular corner graphics and lamps create family resemblance across models.
brand_language_observation: Atlas is moving from rugged ornament toward cleaner functional utility.
designer_note: Track whether future production models consistently apply the modular protection theme.

title: Mira Introduces Soft-Tech Family Face
short_summary: Mock brand-language record about a softer front graphic strategy that combines rounded lamps, reduced intakes, and warm digital details.
design_observations: The front face uses rounded rectangles rather than sharp blades to appear approachable.
Reduced intake graphics help the vehicles read as EV-first.
Warm lighting details make the technology story feel less clinical.
proportion_observation: The family face is designed to work across tall hatchbacks and compact crossovers without forcing a sporty hood line.
volume_observation: Front volumes remain soft and slightly inflated to avoid aggression.
surface_observation: Gentle transitions around the lamps keep the fascia friendly and easy to read.
graphic_observation: Rounded lamp modules are the key brand-recognition device.
brand_language_observation: Mira's mock language favors emotional warmth over sharp technical aggression.
designer_note: Useful for comparing friendly EV front graphics across brands.
